title: Extreme Ownership
theme: The leader owns everything in their world — every outcome, every failure, every gap — with zero excuses and zero blame passed down or sideways.
seed_questions: Where have I blamed a bad outcome on someone else's failure to execute, when the real gap was in how I trained, briefed, or led them?
What is one result in my life right now that I've been explaining away instead of owning?

title: No Bad Teams, Only Bad Leaders
theme: A team's performance is a direct reflection of its leader's standards, attitude, and example — a struggling team is a leadership problem before it's a personnel problem.
seed_questions: If my team, crew, family, or squad is underperforming somewhere, what am I modeling that's producing that?
Have I written off a person as 'the problem' instead of asking what leadership from me could change?

title: Believe
theme: People will not fully commit to a mission until they understand and believe in the reason behind it — a leader must know the 'why' deeply enough to convince others of it.
seed_questions: Do the people who follow me actually understand why we're doing what we're doing, or am I just issuing instructions?
Where in my own life am I going through motions without believing in the mission myself?

title: Check the Ego
theme: Ego clouds judgment, blinds a leader to real conditions, and prevents honest self-assessment — humility and objectivity have to win out over pride for good decisions to follow.
seed_questions: Where has my pride made me defensive instead of teachable this week?
Is there a decision I'm resisting purely because admitting I was wrong would sting?

title: Cover and Move
theme: Teams win through mutual support, not solo heroics — every part of the team is responsible for the success of every other part, because they all fail or succeed together.
seed_questions: Where have I let a silo mentality creep in — treating another team, department, or family member's struggle as 'not my problem'?
Who around me needs me to cover for them this week, even outside my lane?

title: Simple
theme: Plans and instructions have to be stripped down to what's essential and easily understood — complexity breeds confusion, and confusion breeds failure under pressure.
seed_questions: What's one plan, instruction, or expectation I've made needlessly complicated?
If I had to explain today's priority in one sentence to someone tired and distracted, could I?

title: Prioritize and Execute
theme: When multiple problems hit at once, a leader has to relentlessly identify the single highest priority, solve that first, then move to the next — not try to fix everything simultaneously.
seed_questions: What's actually the biggest threat or opportunity in front of me right now, versus what's just loudest?
Where am I scattering my attention across five problems instead of solving the one that matters most?

title: Decentralized Command
theme: No single leader can control everything directly — leaders have to push decision-making authority down to those closest to the problem, and train people to own their own piece of the mission.
seed_questions: Am I holding onto decisions that someone closer to the problem could and should make?
Do the people under my charge understand the mission well enough to make good calls without me in the room?

title: Plan
theme: Good planning means analyzing the mission, identifying every likely contingency, and building a plan the whole team understands and has helped shape — not just issuing top-down orders.
seed_questions: Did I actually plan for this week, or am I just reacting to whatever comes at me?
Who should have had a voice in this plan who didn't?

title: Leading Up and Down the Chain of Command
theme: Leadership isn't just managing subordinates — it's also managing up, making sure those above you have the information and context they need, and asking rather than assuming when guidance is unclear.
seed_questions: Have I kept the people above me (a boss, a commander, a spouse) genuinely informed, or just hoped it would work out?
Where did I assume I understood what was expected of me instead of just asking?

title: Decisiveness Amid Uncertainty
theme: Leaders rarely have complete information — waiting for perfect clarity is itself a decision, usually the wrong one. A good leader gathers what's available, decides, and adjusts as reality unfolds.
seed_questions: What decision have I been stalling on, waiting for certainty that's never going to come?
Where did indecision itself cost me or my team more than a wrong-but-timely call would have?

title: Discipline Equals Freedom
theme: The disciplines that feel restrictive in the moment — routine, structure, standards — are exactly what create the freedom, trust, and capability to handle whatever comes.
seed_questions: What discipline have I let slide that used to give me margin and control?
Where would ten extra minutes of structure today buy me hours of freedom later this week?
